findingsFromThisIndependentReattack.summary: Three condition-phrasing forms outside the prior 9-form matrix - "conditioned upon", "following satisfaction of", and "immediately before and after" (a standalone temporal dual-condition with no accompanying "so long as"/"provided that"/"no Default" connective) - were not matched by source-inventory.ts's CONDITIONAL_PHRASE pattern at all. On a rule where the ONLY conditional-looking language was one of these three forms, and no other reconcilable numeric figure was embedded in the dropped condition text, a silently-dropped condition produced sourceConditionalSignalCount=0, so BLOCKER-9's own >=1 threshold never fired, materialUnresolvedCount stayed 0, and default production routing reached the exact same false clean VERIFIED_NO_MATERIAL_GAP_FOUND outcome BLOCKER-9 was supposed to have eliminated for the general class of qualifying-condition phrasing - just via three different surface forms than the certification's own example.
findingsFromThisIndependentReattack.rootCauseLayer: source-inventory.ts's CONDITIONAL_PHRASE pattern list (Layer 1a - recall, not routing or threshold). Traced independently rather than assumed: reconciliation.ts's threshold (>=1) and verify.ts's shouldInvokeSemanticReview were both already correctly wired and required no change for this specific gap - the signal simply never reached them because Layer 1a's own regex never produced it. This is the SAME layer (not the reconciliation.ts threshold BLOCKER-9 itself fixed) that BLOCKER-9's own remediation doc already fixed once for two other generic forms ("until such time as", "no Event of Default") - this is a continuation of that same, still-incomplete generic-vocabulary coverage, not a new architectural defect.

fix.change: CONDITIONAL_PHRASE pattern extended with three further generic (non-package-specific) alternatives: `conditioned\s+(?:upon|on)`, `(?:following|upon)\s+satisfaction\s+of`, and `immediately\s+before\s+and\s+after`.
fix.why: Each is standard, cross-package credit-agreement drafting vocabulary for a qualifying condition, a precondition-incorporation connective, or a temporal dual-condition test respectively - none is specific to this document's own test sentences (Architecture Invariants #29), matching BLOCKER-9's own established discipline of fixing the general class rather than the one example phrase.

findingsFromThisIndependentReattack.verifiedBy: tests/contract-model/semantic-verification-condition-remediation-rx.test.ts's RECALL/ROUTING/END-TO-END describe blocks for these three forms, plus two dedicated FALSE-POSITIVE GUARDS confirming a correctly-represented condition using either newly-fixed form produces no spurious finding.

findingsFromThisIndependentReattack.summary: A benign, single, unrelated conditional-looking marker anywhere in a candidate's operative source text (e.g. a defined-term/interpretive clause's own incidental "so long as", with no bearing on the compiled rule's actual capacity) correctly and honestly raises reconciliation.ts's coarse AMBIGUOUS/UNCERTAIN condition signal per BLOCKER-9's own intended, disclosed design ("a single ambiguous marker... belongs to be resolved [at Layer 2]") - that part is working exactly as BLOCKER-9 intended, not a bug. The actual defect: once Layer 2 is invoked and a REAL, independent, non-synthetic adversarial reviewer examines the exact same source text and deterministic signal (both are in its prompt per reviewer.ts's buildUserContent) and reports NOTHING wrong at all, the candidate's final status was PERMANENTLY stuck at REVIEW_REQUIRED - never resolving to a confirmed-clean state - because verify.ts's mergeFindings/maxSeverity can only ever RAISE a deterministic UNCERTAIN finding's severity via a matching semantic finding, never LOWER it via a genuine confirming "nothing wrong" verdict. This is not a hypothetical: this document's own new benign-case test demonstrated it concretely BEFORE the fix below, using a scripted non-synthetic reviewer returning findings:[] (the same wire shape a real model would return for an honest clean pass). Before BLOCKER-9, this same underlying mechanism existed but needed >=2 independent stray markers to fire for the condition/exception signal specifically, making it far rarer; BLOCKER-9's own >=1 threshold makes this reachable from a single, very common stray word, so real production traffic will now hit permanent REVIEW_REQUIRED for benign single markers meaningfully more often than before BLOCKER-9's fix - a genuine, serious precision cost of that fix that was not previously measured or disclosed.
findingsFromThisIndependentReattack.rootCauseLayer: verify.ts's orchestration layer (mergeFindings/determineStatus), specifically the absence of ANY mechanism by which a genuine Layer 2 confirmation (of either kind: confirming the concern OR confirming its absence) can resolve a Layer-1-only coarse AMBIGUOUS/UNCERTAIN finding downward. Not reconciliation.ts's threshold (correctly >=1, left unchanged - reverting it would reopen BLOCKER-9), not findings.ts's severity mapping (AMBIGUOUS-is-always-UNCERTAIN-until-confirmed is correct and was deliberately left unchanged), not the routing decision in shouldInvokeSemanticReview (correctly and conservatively invokes Layer 2 for this shape, left unchanged), and not the AI verifier's own prompt (already asks it to investigate the deterministic signal). The defect is specifically that 'pending Layer 2 confirmation' (findings.ts's own documented language) never actually gets resolved either way by verify.ts once Layer 2 completes.

files.change: SemanticReviewResult gained a new `isSynthetic: boolean` field (threaded straight from the calling StageCaller's own existing `isSynthetic` flag), returned on both the success and failure paths of runAdversarialSemanticReview.

Added downgradeUnconfirmedAmbiguousFindings, called immediately after mergeFindings inside the needsSemanticReview branch. It downgrades a finding from UNCERTAIN to NON_MATERIAL (never deletes it - full audit trail preserved, resolutionStatus stays OPEN for human review) only when ALL of: (1) the finding is still purely DETERMINISTIC_ONLY (a finding Layer 2 actually merged into, confirming it, is never touched - its severity already correctly reflects the confirmation via maxSeverity); (2) its exact verifierReasoning string matches one of reconciliation.items' own AMBIGUOUS-classification reason strings (never a hard NOT_ACCOUNTED_FOR/IR_ONLY numeric-evidence finding, identified this way specifically so real numeric evidence keeps its severity unconditionally, regardless of whether a model call happens to notice it - BLOCKER-9's own recall guarantee is preserved with zero exception); (3) the review that ran was genuinely non-synthetic (review.isSynthetic === false) - the no-credential SyntheticStageCaller fallback's inevitable empty response must never be mistaken for an independent confirmation, which is exactly why isSynthetic was threaded through in this same fix; (4) the review did not itself independently report ANY finding of the same findingType for this candidate (which would mean it DID confirm the concern - in that case the signal is left exactly alone, and the confirming finding's own severity, not this one, drives status).

fix.why: Fixes the specific, demonstrated defect (a real confirming-clean Layer 2 review cannot ever move an AMBIGUOUS-origin UNCERTAIN finding off REVIEW_REQUIRED) without touching reconciliation.ts's threshold, findings.ts's severity mapping, or the routing decision - BLOCKER-9's own fix and disposition (REMEDIATED_PENDING_INDEPENDENT_RECERTIFICATION) remain fully intact and unmodified. A genuine material omission is never masked: this document's own 'genuine MATERIAL omission is never masked' test drives the exact same code path with a reviewer that DOES confirm the omission, and confirms status still reaches MATERIAL_DISCREPANCY.

independencePreservation.claim: Verifier independence is preserved by both fixes in this document - no compiler reasoning trace, hidden reasoning, prompt conclusion, confidence score, or benchmark ground truth was given to the verifier as evidence of correctness, and the precision fix specifically distinguishes a genuine independent adversarial judgment (real or realistically-scripted, non-synthetic) from a no-op stub, rather than ever short-circuiting on anything the compiler itself asserts.
evidence: source-inventory.ts's three new pattern alternatives operate purely on raw operativeSourceText, exactly like every existing pattern in that file - no compiler output, IR, or reasoning trace is consulted.

verify.ts's downgradeUnconfirmedAmbiguousFindings consults only: (a) reconciliation.ts's own already-computed, source-and-IR-only ReconciliationResult (specifically, which of its OWN classifications were AMBIGUOUS - a fact about Layer 1's own output, not the compiler's), and (b) the Layer 2 reviewer's own returned findings and isSynthetic flag - never compilationResult.overallNotes/sufficiencyReasons/unresolvedIssues or any other compiler-conclusion field the Independence Contract at the top of semantic-verification/types.ts forbids.

prompt.ts (the AI verifier's own instructions) was not modified by either fix in this document - the reviewer is told nothing different about what to conclude; it is simply given a chance to be believed when it explicitly confirms nothing is wrong, exactly as its own existing prompt already asks it to 'investigate each' deterministic signal.

Re-ran tests/contract-model/semantic-verification-independence.test.ts (the mechanical enforcement test: a static regex-over-import-lines check that nothing under lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-verification/** imports semantic/compile.ts's compileCovenantToIR or semantic/caller.ts's RealSemanticCaller/getSemanticCaller) after both fixes - all 3 tests still PASS, confirming the fixed files introduce no forbidden import.

The precision fix's own synthetic-fallback guard (isSynthetic) is itself an independence-preserving safeguard, not a weakening of it: it specifically prevents a no-op stub (which never read a single word of real source text) from ever being credited with an adversarial judgment it never made.

This is recorded as an open observation, not a fix: a future adversarial pass finding a genuine bare-"pro forma compliance"-only real-world clause should re-test this specific gap before assuming it is closed by this document.
dispositionRationale: This independent re-attack of BLOCKER-9's own fix, using 12 condition-phrasing forms deliberately disjoint from the prior 9-form matrix plus 5 benign/precision cases, found the fix's core mechanism (reconciliation.ts's >=1 threshold, routed through verify.ts's unchanged shouldInvokeSemanticReview) generalizes correctly to every new material form tested, but also found two genuine, independently-root-caused defects: (1) a recall gap in source-inventory.ts's CONDITIONAL_PHRASE vocabulary for three further generic condition-phrasing forms, and (2) a serious precision regression in verify.ts's orchestration layer, where a benign single stray marker (made substantially more likely to matter by BLOCKER-9's own threshold change) could never resolve off REVIEW_REQUIRED even after a genuine, independent Layer 2 reviewer confirmed nothing was wrong. Both are now fixed, at the layer that actually produced each defect, without reverting or weakening BLOCKER-9's own >=1 threshold or its ir-inventory.ts companion fix - both remain fully intact. All 43 new tests, all 30 prior-matrix tests, all 29 fault-injection tests (including every false-positive guard), and the full 1155-test contract-model suite pass; tsc/eslint show zero new errors against the documented baseline; verifier independence remains mechanically enforced and unmodified in substance. Per this workstream's own instructions, disposition is REMEDIATED_PENDING_INDEPENDENT_RECERTIFICATION, not CERTIFIED_CLOSED - that verdict is reserved for a future, genuinely independent recertification pass this document is not, and given that this very re-attack itself found two new defects in a fix that a prior phase had already run 30 passing tests against, a further independent pass on THIS document's own fixes before any CERTIFIED_CLOSED verdict is warranted, not merely procedurally required.
